items.content_html: As Gamescom 2026 opens in Cologne, AI, hardware costs and slowing user growth are putting pressure on the global games industry despite its current strength.

items.title: Why Germany's Volkswagen could cut 100,000 jobs
items.content_html: Europe's biggest automaker, Volkswagen, faces Chinese competition, high costs and US tariffs. What could its restructuring mean for the German car industry?

items.title: Can new US sanctions cripple Iran's shadow economy?
items.content_html: The US is expanding sanctions on Iran's financial networks, targeting crypto, gold, aviation and shipping. DW spoke with analysts about what could change.

items.title: Trees are vital for cooler cities, but they need help too
items.content_html: Record-breaking heat and drought are putting urban trees at risk. Experts explain how to protect these essential assets and build city forests that can withstand the climate challenges ahead.

items.title: Scientists discover new 'immune hubs' in skull bone marrow
items.content_html: "Immune hubs" that actively defend the brain have been discovered in mouse skull marrow. Similar cells exist in human skulls, but their role remains unclear.

items.title: Spiraling health costs force Iranians to delay care
items.content_html: A single chemotherapy session in Iran can cost six times the monthly minimum wage. As drug prices soar and medicine is in short supply, doctors say more patients are delaying or abandoning treatment.
